blurb: Bob-tailed French bird dog that points and retrieves, named for the Brittany region
description: The Brittany Spaniel is a medium-sized French gun dog from Brittany, bred for bird hunting, with a short or absent tail and a pied, roan or tri-colour coat.
answer: The Brittany Spaniel, or Épagneul Breton, is a French gun dog of spaniel type bred mainly for bird hunting. It developed in Brittany in north-west France between the seventeenth and nineteenth centuries. It is a medium-sized, cobby dog standing about 45 to 53 cm, often with a naturally short tail.

body: Orange-and-white dogs of similar type appear hunting and retrieving game in seventeenth-century tapestries and paintings. In 1850 Reverend Davies described small bobtailed dogs that pointed and retrieved well, and around that time the breed was crossed with English Setters. It was first recognised in France in 1907. The American Kennel Club approved it in 1934 and dropped Spaniel from the name in 1982.

The breed has a spaniel-type head, a cobby build and a tail that may be short, absent or of normal length. The coat may be black-and-white, orange-and-white or liver-and-white, pied or roan, or tri-coloured; solid colours are not accepted. The American Brittany is bred somewhat larger, with a blockier head, standing 44 to 52 cm and weighing 14 to 18 kg under the AKC standard.
The source text says little about temperament. The breed is described above all as a working bird dog that both points and retrieves.
Sources give little specific detail on care. As a hunting breed developed for fieldwork, it is generally thought to need regular, vigorous exercise and mental stimulation.

A 2015 French study found a median longevity of 12.6 years, and a 2024 UK study found 11.1 years. Conditions reported in the breed include hip dysplasia, which one North American study found at 4.22% compared with 3.52% overall, and glaucoma at a slightly higher-than-average rate. Its rate of elbow dysplasia was among the lowest of 60 breeds studied.

faq.q: Is a Brittany a spaniel or a pointer?
faq.a: It is a spaniel-type gun dog, but it was bred to point game birds as well as retrieve them.

faq.q: How big does a Brittany Spaniel get?
faq.a: It typically stands about 45 to 53 cm at the withers. The American type is somewhat larger and weighs around 14 to 18 kg.

faq.q: How long do Brittany Spaniels live?
faq.a: Studies have found median longevity of 12.6 years in France and 11.1 years in the UK.

faq.q: Is the Brittany Spaniel recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. It is FCI breed number 95 in Group 7, Pointing Dogs.
